## Regression bisect: introduced by `d39290fbb9` (PR #47753, 2026-09-09)

I traced the history of `packages/desktop/src/main/wsl/runtime.ts` and found the exact change that turned this into a release regression.

**Culprit commit:** `d39290fbb9a57c442fd8a51f2e147b50a81178d8` — *feat(desktop): add SSH server connections (#47753)*, authored 2026-09-09. That PR refactored the WSL CLI resolution/installation to reuse the new shared `RemoteCli` helpers written for SSH — where arguments are not re-expanded by `wsl.exe`. The WSL path inherited scripts that depend on runtime shell expansion, and that is what breaks.

Git confirms `d39290fbb9` is an ancestor of every V2 desktop release so far: **v2.0.0 (2026-09-11), v2.0.1 and v2.0.2 (2026-09-12)**. The 1.18.x line is unaffected (different code path).

### The two changes that break WSL

**1) Detection — `resolveWslCli()`**

Before #47753 the embedded script only referenced `$HOME`, which WSL's pre-expansion replaces with the correct value anyway:

```ts
return firstLine(
  (
    await runWslSh(
      'if [ -x "$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode2" ]; then printf "%s\\n" "$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode2"; fi',
      distro,
      opts,
    )
  ).stdout,
)
```

After #47753 it becomes `RemoteCli.discoverScript()`, which depends on a **runtime** shell variable:

```sh
cli=""
if [ -z "$cli" ] && [ -x "$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode" ]; then cli="$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode"; fi

if [ -n "$cli" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$cli"; fi
```

Under WSL's argument pre-expansion `$cli` is replaced with the empty string *before* `sh` runs, so the final condition is always false and `resolveWslCli()` always returns empty → "OpenCode not installed" forever.

**2) Install verification — `wslCliInstallCommand()`**

Before #47753 the install command was a plain `curl | bash` with **no verification step**. After #47753 it uses `RemoteCli.installScript()`, which appends:

```sh
test "$("$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode" --version | awk '{print $NF}' | sed 's/^v//')" = '2.0.2'
```

The command substitution and `$NF` are consumed by the same pre-expansion pass; `sh` actually receives `test "" = '2.0.2'`, so the install reports failure *after* the binary has already been installed successfully.

### Verification (same Node `child_process.spawn` call the Electron main process uses)

| Script form | Output on `wsl -d Debian -- sh -lc <script>` |
| --- | --- |
| Pre-#47753 form (only `$HOME`) | `/home/<user>/.opencode/bin/opencode` ✅ |
| `RemoteCli.discoverScript()` (post-#47753) | empty ❌ |

Tested with WSL 2.6.1.0, Windows 11 build 26200, Debian (WSL2).

### Suggested fix (targets this regression specifically)

- Route the WSL scripts through **stdin** instead of argv (the pattern `packages/desktop/src/main/wsl/sidecar.ts` already uses), or
- Add `--exec`/`-e` in `wslArgs()` so the arguments bypass the default Linux shell;
- Keep the shared `RemoteCli` scripts for SSH only, or teach them an "arguments are not expanded" mode.

Happy to provide the full cmdline dumps or a repro script if useful.

Closing as a duplicate of #42700 (`tui: leaks ~21MB .so per launch into /tmp; fills tmpfs and breaks TUI startup`), which already covers this across all install channels (npm, standalone, curl) and platforms (Linux .so / macOS .dylib).

Root cause confirmed there: opencode's binary (a Bun standalone executable) embeds OpenTUI's `libopentui.so` (Zig-built), and Bun's `bun:ffi` loader re-extracts it to a uniquely-named temp file on every load via bunfs, never cleaning up. Files are byte-identical (same size + md5), and none are held open by live processes.

Fix status: resolved in OpenCode V2 (uses Bun 1.4.0-canary.1 with oven-sh/bun#29587, content-hash-cached extraction). V1 (1.18.x) is still affected — keep a periodic purge until upgrading.

I implemented the same change locally and verified it end-to-end. Two notes that might be useful:

**Filtering the list isn't enough on its own.** `Skill.available()` is the only model-facing list — its sole caller is `session/system.ts` — so filtering there hides the skill from `<available_skills>` while leaving slash commands working, since command discovery uses `Skill.all()`. But both skill tools still resolve by name from the full registry: v1 `tool/skill.ts` calls `.require(params.name)`, v2 `core/src/tool/skill.ts` calls `skills.list().find(...)`. A model that knows the name can load it regardless. Your PR patches both tool files, which is the right call — worth keeping.

Measured on a config with 122 skills, 19 of them flagged: `debug skill` (the `all()` path) still lists all 122, the model-visible list drops to 103, and the difference is exactly those 19 — no collateral filtering.

**Plugins that register their own `skill` tool bypass this entirely.** I hit it locally: with a plugin overriding the tool, the refusal never fired even after patching both native tools. The tell was the tool output wording not matching anything in the opencode source. Probably out of scope for this PR, but it may be worth a line in `skills.mdx`, since plugin-provided skill tools are fairly common.

Hi, I created Multiuser Opencode, please have a look: https://github.com/cahya-wirawan/opencode-multiuser

The project turns OpenCode into a centrally managed, multi-user developer platform for enterprise and internal engineering environments. It provides authenticated access to isolated, disposable OpenCode workspaces while keeping project files and OpenCode state persistent across container restarts.

Instead of giving every developer a permanently running VM or asking users to manage OpenCode locally, the platform allocates an isolated rootless Podman container only when a workspace is needed. A central FastAPI control plane handles authentication (using local user/password or OIDC), authorization, workspace lifecycle, routing, capacity limits, idle cleanup, and administrative controls. Traefik exposes a single portal URL, while OpenCode itself remains unmodified upstream software.

## Suppressing the automatic browser open of `opencode web`, without touching opencode code

### Problem
When running `opencode web`, the server automatically opens the default browser. There is no flag to disable this (`opencode web --help` offers none). We run opencode as a headless service behind our own auth/proxy layer and don't want the browser to pop up on every restart.

### Diagnosis
`opencode web` serves the web UI from an embedded Node.js server, which uses the `open` npm package to launch the browser. On Linux that package invokes `xdg-open` (or `sensible-browser` on WSL/Debian) via `PATH`. Two things make this hard to control:

- the environment variable `$BROWSER` is ignored on plain Linux by the `open` package,
- there is no CLI switch to suppress the open.

### Solution adopted – a PATH shim (zero changes to opencode)
Since `open` locates the browser launcher exclusively through `PATH`, we prepend a shim directory to `PATH` *only for the opencode process*. The shim directory contains a no-op script reachable under every name the launcher might try: `xdg-open`, `sensible-browser`, `x-www-browser`, `gvfs-open` and `open` (symlinks to a single `open-nothing` script).

Result: `opencode web` starts, the server comes up on its port, and the "open browser" call is silently swallowed (exit code 0, so opencode keeps running normally). The suppressed call is logged to `logs/browser-open.log` for debugging.

Example (our `start.sh` does this for the core process):

```bash
NO_BROWSER_DIR="$PWD/.nobrowser"      # contains open-nothing + symlinks
BROWSER_LOG="$PWD/logs/browser-open.log"

# open-nothing:
#!/bin/sh
echo "[shim $(basename $0)] $*" >> "$BROWSER_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
exit 0

# start opencode web with the shim in front of PATH:
PATH="$NO_BROWSER_DIR:$PATH" BROWSER="$NO_BROWSER_DIR/xdg-open" opencode web --port 4986
```

The `BROWSER` assignment is belt-and-braces for the cases where the package *does* honour it.

An `OC_OPEN_BROWSER=1` env toggle re-enables the normal browser open.

### Limitations
- It is a workaround, not a feature: anything else the child process spawns also sees the stubbed `xdg-open` (acceptable here, since it is only applied to the one process).
- Because `$BROWSER` is not honoured on plain Linux, a shim on `PATH` is the only easy interception point – hence stubbing several launcher names.

## Same symptom reproduced on the v2.0.2 **stable** line — one full local MCP set per directory, and the #46828 browse fix is not present in 2.0.x

### Environment

- opencode **v2.0.2** (`@opencode/cli`, pnpm global), running `opencode serve --service`
- Linux `6.18.49-2-lts` x86_64
- User-scope config with 3 local stdio MCP servers (`mysql` + `postgres` via `@bytebase/dbhub`, `jetbrains` via `supergateway`) plus 1 remote (`context7`)

### Deterministic reproduction (one request)

Reading any directory through the location-scoped fs endpoint used by the picker materializes a full Location runtime and starts a complete set of local MCP servers for that directory.

1. Record the baseline of MCP-related processes under the service.
2. Call the picker's endpoint for a single directory:
   `GET /api/fs/list?location[directory]=/tmp/opencode`
3. Within ~8 seconds the service spawns a new set of every local MCP server:

```
BEFORE: 8 MCP-related processes
GET /api/fs/list?location[directory]=/tmp/opencode -> 200
AFTER:  14 MCP-related processes (delta +6)

627672 579141 220180  npm exec @bytebase/dbhub@latest --dsn mysql://...***...
627673 579141 197480  npm exec supergateway --sse http://127.0.0.1:64343/sse
627674 579141 193580  npm exec @bytebase/dbhub@latest --dsn postgres://...***...
628094 627672 150616  node .../dbhub --dsn mysql://...***...
628101 627673 100344  node .../supergateway --sse http://127.0.0.1:64343/sse
628107 627674 150452  node .../dbhub --dsn postgres://...***...
```

That is roughly **1 GB RSS added per directory visited**. Browsing a directory tree with N children starts N of these sets. All spawned processes are direct children of the service PID and are not cleaned up.

### The fix for #46826 is not in v2.0.2

#46828 (which closed #46826 and #46679) added `GET /api/browse/list` so the workspace picker and `/cd` navigate without resolving a Location. On v2.0.2:

- `GET /api/browse/list` returns **404**
- the shipped binary contains **no `browse` route** at all (only `api/fs/list`, `api/fs/find`, `api/fs/read/`)
- the full `/openapi.json` (122 routes) has no `browse` entry

So on 2.0.x, directory browsing still goes through `fs/list` -> `LocationMiddleware`, the exact mechanism described in #46826 and #37844.

### Ask

Was #46828 intended to land in the 2.0.x stable line? If yes, could it be picked/re-landed? If 2.0.x deliberately uses a different navigation path, what is the expected behavior when a browsed directory inherits user-scope local MCP servers?

Related: #46826, #46828, #46679, #37844

## Additional deterministic reproduction from Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#3318

I reproduced this on OpenCode `1.18.18` with a disposable localhost-only provider endpoint and a passive plugin-hook trace. No credentials, prompts, raw output, or private repository data were recorded.

| Child outcome | Parent/plugin observation |
|---|---|
| Valid non-empty text | Foreground task completed with a non-empty task result. |
| Successful result with no text parts | Parent-facing completed task result was empty. |
| Malformed nested task result | The consumer plugin received enough output to classify it as malformed. |
| Child HTTP 400 provider error | OpenCode emitted `session.error`, but the parent/plugin boundary still received the empty-result shape. |
| Background task | The running acknowledgement arrived once through `tool.execute.after`; terminal completion arrived later through synthetic parent-message injection. |

For the provider-error case, this confirms the distinction described in this issue: the child error exists in host events, but the foreground parent-facing Task result loses that distinction and looks empty.

At tag `v1.18.18` (`31406ccc51b4bd2a4e1e086b2bcaa5f7f804f26d`), `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts` derives the child result from the last text part and falls back to `""`. The downstream Gentle AI SDD plugin therefore cannot distinguish a genuine no-text completion from this provider-error transport loss; it can only fail closed on the already-collapsed value.

The full consumer-side report and sanitized outcome matrix are tracked at Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#3318. This comment is reproduction evidence only; it does not claim that every empty task result has the same upstream cause.

For anyone running into severe SSE event stream memory ballooning as described here:

I created an experimental personal fork with workaround bounds: https://github.com/qvkap/opencode-clean

**Disclaimer**:
- This contains AI-assisted heuristic patches ("AI slop").
- I am aware that project maintainers have requested contributors not to submit LLM-generated code or bugfixes upstream; this is not submitted as an official PR or recommendation.
- This is NOT a complete or definitive solution. It only mitigates roughly ~20% of the memory exhaustion surface by putting defensive bounds on queues and diagnostic caches.
- Deep runtime leaks (such as EventTarget listener accumulation in the bundled AI-SDK Effect runtime and Bun/V8 heap retention under heavy tool usage) remain unaddressed.

**Mitigation applied for this issue**:
In `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/event.ts`, `Queue.unbounded<EventV2.Payload>()` was replaced with `Queue.sliding<EventV2.Payload>(1_000)` to prevent the worker process from accumulating gigabytes of unconsumed events when downstream consumers lag. Additional LRU caps (`MAX_DIAGNOSTICS_FILES = 5_000`, `MAX_OPEN_FILES = 1_000`) were placed on the LSP client state.

Under moderate single-session use this prevents the worker from spiking to 9+ GB as quickly, though long-running heavy sessions will still eventually require restarting until a proper runtime-level fix lands upstream.

Good question, and I think it's the one that decides whether the timeout path is usable rather than merely safe.

Concretely, in the thing I built: the ask is a durable record, not a transient push. The call returns an id, the pending question keeps existing after the wait window closes, and it stays answerable — so "was this ever decided, and which way" is a lookup on that id afterwards, from either side. Someone opening the app late finds the question still sitting there rather than discovering it evaporated.

But I'd pull apart two things your comment holds together, because only one of them is the approval layer's job:

1. Did the human ever answer, and what did they say. An approval channel can and should guarantee this, and it's cheap — a stable id plus a record that outlives the wait window.
2. What the run actually did after NO ANSWER. It can't. The approval layer knows the answer was "nothing"; it has no idea what the harness then chose to do. And if the same layer that blocked the action also blocked the read, as you describe, no notification service fixes that — the harness has to emit that state itself.
Which I think reinforces your point about who owns the retry decision. The operator needs (2) to make it, and (2) can only come from opencode, not from whatever channel carried the question.

## Follow-up: not `@ai-sdk/xai`; provider `websocket: false` is ignored for Grok

Reproduced on **2.0.2** after setting `providers.xai.websocket: false`. Live `GET /api/provider/xai` returned `"websocket": false`, then a new session still died with the same error.

Babysit session `ses_f6906ee09ffeEfVdKX2PPKsh4o` (`xai/grok-4.6#medium`, prompt `get to work`): start 2026-09-12T18:55:00Z → `provider.transport` **WebSocket closed with code 1006** at 18:58:30Z (~3.5 min, many tool/image rounds). `idle_outcome=failed`.

### Where the error is actually thrown

Exact message is OpenCode’s own transport, **v2.0.2** `packages/ai/src/route/transport/websocket.ts`:

```ts
transportError(`WebSocket closed with code ${event.code}`, {
  operation: "read",
  code: String(event.code),
  phase: "close",
})
```

That is `@opencode/ai` `WebSocketExecutor` on the Responses WebSocket (`wss://…/v1/responses`), not a TUI↔server socket.

### `@ai-sdk/xai` is not the chat WebSocket

Checked `vercel/ai` `packages/xai` (published `@ai-sdk/xai@4.0.58`):

- Chat / Responses use HTTP `fetch` only (OpenCode’s `provider-xai-responses.test.ts` mocks `fetch` on `.responses()`).
- SDK WebSockets are for streaming STT / realtime, not Grok coding turns.

### Why provider-level `websocket: false` does nothing on xAI

`XAIPlugin` stamps **every** xAI model (`packages/core/src/plugin/provider/xai.ts`):

```ts
draft.capabilities.responsesWebsockets = true
draft.websocket = true
```

Catalog merge is `model.websocket ?? provider.websocket` (`packages/core/src/catalog.ts`). Model `true` wins, so provider `false` is ignored. `ModelResolver` uses `selected.websocket`. Test `enables xAI Responses WebSockets` expects `grok-4.6.websocket === true`.

`ConfigProviderPlugin` runs later (`post`) but only writes `model.websocket` when set **on the model**. Same stamp exists on OpenAI models.

Expected working config:

```jsonc
{
  "providers": {
    "xai": {
      "websocket": false,
      "models": {
        "grok-4.6": { "websocket": false }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Provider-only `false` is a documented no-op for Grok until the plugin stops forcing model-level `true`, or merge treats provider `false` as an override.

Still needed: treat mid-stream close 1006 as retryable `Transport` (`operation: "read"`) and HTTP-fallback when no output is committed.

Still reproducing on the current release (1.18.30, Linux), and it is not limited to local models or to one provider.

I run a local LLM router (key rotation and fallback toward cloud providers) and OpenCode talks to it directly on localhost, so I can see both sides of every request. I hit this with Alibaba Model Studio (qwen3.8-max, reasoning_effort medium) and with Perplexity's agent API (claude family reasoning models). The common factor is any upstream that thinks silently for more than 300s before the first byte. While the upstream has produced no response headers there is nothing for the router to forward, and Desktop kills the request at exactly five minutes.

Router side logs from one evening (time from request receipt to client socket close; not a single response byte had been sent on any of these):

    2026-09-11 17:01  300002 ms
    2026-09-11 18:16  300008 ms
    2026-09-11 18:49  300010 ms
    2026-09-12 20:00  300002 ms
    2026-09-12 20:06  299974 ms
    2026-09-12 20:32  299992 ms

Every abort lands at 300.0s within about 20ms. After each death the client retries (the next attempt starts about 2s after the previous one died, which matches SessionRetry with RETRY_INITIAL_DELAY = 2000 and RETRY_MAX_RETRIES = 5), and the retry dies the same way. A single prompt can burn half an hour across a chain of identical attempts before the user sees an error.

The provider UA on these requests reports runtime/node.js/24, so it is the Electron sidecar running the Node server bundle, where global fetch is undici.

Two layers are involved on 1.18.30:

1. With default config, OpenCode's own timer fires first. In packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:

       const headerTimeout = options["headerTimeout"] ?? 300_000

   which aborts with ProviderError.HeaderTimeoutError ("Provider response headers timed out after 300000ms"). That part is documented and intentional.

2. The escape hatch does not work on Desktop. Raising the value or setting "headerTimeout": false only removes OpenCode's timer. The sidecar's fetch is still Node's undici with its default 300s headersTimeout, and nothing in the codebase configures a dispatcher (there is no setGlobalDispatcher call anywhere; the timeout: false passed in provider.ts is a Bun only option, the ts-ignore right above it links to an oven-sh/bun issue). So on Desktop a request can never wait more than 300s for response headers, regardless of config, while the CLI on Bun honors the setting. That is the asymmetry people in this thread were told to work around by using the CLI.

The same wall also appears mid stream, which is the clearest confirmation that this is a transport level inactivity timer and not an application timeout: with slow reasoning models, a stream that has already started dies the same way when no bytes arrive for 300s (undici's bodyTimeout). When my router emits an SSE comment line (": keepalive") every 15s, the same streams survive the silence and complete normally.

Same root cause as the original report (the "Headers Timeout Error" there is undici's HeadersTimeoutError), observed here from the server side. Closed weight reasoning models routinely take minutes before the first streamed byte now, so the 300s wall gets hit in normal daily use on Desktop, with remote providers as well as local models.

PR #33535 had the right fix (map the provider timeout options to an undici Agent with headersTimeout: 0 / bodyTimeout: 0 when running on Node) but it was closed by the automated cleanup without a review. Is there appetite to land something like that? I can test a build against the router setup above and report back.

Correction to my earlier comment above, and a much more precise picture of the actual blocker.

**I need to retract the central claim I made on 2026-08-30.** I wrote that "looking at the last 500 merged PRs in this repo: **zero** were authored by external (non-org) contributors," and that none of the external fork PRs "appear to have ever had their required CI run." Both statements are wrong, and I am sorry for adding noise to this thread with them.

Checking the last 100 merged PRs, **30 were authored by contributors outside the core team**, including v2-targeted merges by `dajiaohuang` (#48452) and `Tarquinen` (#48249). I verified both accounts have no organization membership, so they are genuinely external, and **both merged with 0 reviews**. So the repository is not closed to external contributions, and I should not have implied that it was.

**The real blocker is narrower, and it is mechanical.** The `v2` ruleset (id `19434226`, active) requires five status checks before merge:

```
unit (linux), unit (windows), e2e (linux), e2e (windows), typecheck
```

`required_approving_review_count` is `0`, and the only allowed merge method is squash. Those checks are produced by the `test` workflow, which triggers on `pull_request`. For **first-time contributors from a fork**, that workflow stays at `completed/action_required` until a maintainer approves it — so it never runs.

That creates a genuinely misleading signal. `gh pr checks` only lists checks that actually executed:

```
$ gh pr checks 43460
check-compliance  pass   # pull_request_target, no approval needed
check-standards   pass   # pull_request_target, no approval needed
```

It looks green. But the five required checks are simply absent, so `mergeStateStatus` is `BLOCKED` and the PR can never satisfy the ruleset. The workflow runs on that PR have been sitting in `action_required` since 2026-08-25:

```
32837016989 | test      | completed/action_required | 2026-08-25T10:23
32837016988 | typecheck | completed/action_required | 2026-08-25T10:23
```

Compare with an in-repo branch PR (#47529), whose check list includes the full set.

**Why I cannot resolve this myself**: my token has `push: false` and `triage: false` on this repository, and a fork author cannot approve their own workflow runs either. `GET /repos/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs?status=action_required` currently returns a queue of runs in this state from several other external contributors as well (woodsonl, shinelon, muhamedbeshir, prethiv, mehmetmalli, mblakele, xiaoguomeiyitian, ...), so this is a pattern rather than something specific to my PRs.

**The one action that unblocks it** is a maintainer clicking "Approve and run" on the pending runs for a fork PR. After that the required checks execute normally and the ruleset can be satisfied. If the project would rather not approve runs ad hoc, a ruleset or workflow change that runs the required checks automatically for fork PRs would fix this class of problem for every external contributor at once.

For reference, the work waiting on this: #43282 (base `v2`, fixes #36761) and #43460 (base `v2`). For #43282 the checks additionally cannot pass until the branch is rebased onto `v2`, which I am unable to do while my git write access is unavailable.
